result.title: Bridging Teacher-Student Capability Gaps with Recurrent Computation
result.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers capabilities from large language models to smaller students, yet stronger teachers do not always yield better students. Recent studies report diminishing or even negative returns from teacher scaling. We hypothesize that these limitations arise in part from insufficient student capacity to absorb the teacher's knowledge. We therefore investigate loop and recurrent computation as a way to expand the student's effective capacity by modifying its computation graph while keeping the backbone parameter count fixed. Under teacher-forced KD during pretraining, weight-shared looping improves performance but retains teacher-size saturation, whereas cross-token recurrence avoids the observed reversal with larger teachers. In mathematical post-training under both teacher-forced KD and on-policy distillation (OPD), recurrent students scale better with increasing teacher size than looped and vanilla LLMs do. Crucially, we show that a pretrained LLM can be readily fine-tuned into a looped or recurrent architecture jointly with OPD, without repeating pretraining. Our recurrent Qwen model improves with larger teachers and consistently outperforms looped and vanilla LLMs. This suggests a new post-training paradigm that integrates architectural conversion into distillation, avoiding a separate conversion stage while substantially improving student performance and maintaining near-vanilla inference latency.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对教师规模增大时蒸馏收益递减甚至反转的问题，提出在固定主干参数下用 weight-shared looping 与 cross-token recurrence 扩展学生的有效容量，并在预训练 KD 与数学后训练的教师强制 KD/OPD 中比较两者，还展示了把预训练 LLM 直接微调为循环架构的路径。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽为纯文本蒸馏工作，但其对「loop 式与跨 token 递归」的区分、递归深度与容量吸收关系以及近 vanilla 推理延迟，可能为 LVR 的循环状态更新与动态计算成本提供可核查的方法线索。
